subject: Throughput commitments and cross-site egress choreography for BrightLane private GPU pools
messages:
From: Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.com>
To: Priya Shah <priya@brightlane.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 6 Oct 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Throughput commitments and cross-site egress choreography for BrightLane private GPU pools

Hi Priya —

Thanks again for the call this morning. Per request, attaching a concise capacity model and a short checklist so your infra team can validate networking before we kick off the provisioning window. High-level ask/questions below so we can lock the SLA commitments for the pilot: 

Summary points (pilot targets):
- Sustained throughput target: 20k tokens/sec aggregate (across two availability sites) during business hours (PST).
- Peak absorbable burst: 45k tokens/sec for up to 3 minutes (expected traffic spikes).
- Warm pool sizing: maintain a 15% warm pool across GPU nodes to avoid cold-KV misses.
- Failover RTO target: 90s for routing+cache-warm on cross-site failover.

Network/economics considerations we need you to confirm:
1) Egress path: will production requests exit via your on-prem edge or via BrightLane’s cloud egress? Please confirm where NAT/Egress IPs will be announced.
2) Inter-site bandwidth: we recommend 10 Gbps dedicated cross-site link for model KV sync and checkpoint replication. If you only have 1–2 Gbps available, we’ll need to reduce cross-site sync frequency and raise failover window.
3) MTU/packet pacing: for sustained token rates, jumbo frames (9000 MTU) reduce CPU overhead on the GPU hosts — check if your switches permit this end-to-end.

What we attached: capacity-model-v2.xlsx (striped scenarios: baseline / 2x growth / 5x growth) — please share the baseline telemetry (avg request size, tokens per request) so we can pin the right pod size.

Requested next steps:
- Priya: confirm egress topology + estimated average tokens/request by Fri 10/8.
- Laura: we'll coordinate the provisioning calendar once we have confirmed bandwidth.
- Jonas/Naomi: review failover steps and flag any operational blockers.

If helpful I can schedule a 30-minute technical handoff with your network ops and our infra team.

Thanks,
Diego Fernandez
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference

Attachment: capacity-model-v2.xlsx (spreadsheet, ~120KB)
From: Priya Shah <priya@brightlane.com>
To: Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.com>
Cc: ops@brightlane.com
Date: Wed, 7 Oct 2026 14:03:12 -0700
Subject: Re: Throughput commitments and cross-site egress choreography for BrightLane private GPU pools

Diego —

Appreciate the clear breakdown. Quick answers from ops:
- Egress: production traffic exits via BrightLane egress (NAT at our edge), public egress IPs will be managed by us. We can announce a /29 for the service.
- Inter-site: current links are 2 x 10 Gbps but cross-site latency varies (6–12 ms). We can carve out a VLAN and guarantee 6 Gbps for the cluster.
- MTU: switches support 9000 MTU; we will verify end-to-end on Thursday.

Tokens/request: on average ~850 tokens/request for our current chat flows, bursty during morning and evening syncs. If you recommend profiling, we can provide 48 hours of traffic from prod (anonymized).

Two clarifying questions:
1) Egress billing — will traffic between our VPC (on-prem) and Redwood control plane count toward the pilot’s egress estimate? We need to understand cost exposure before committing to the baseline.
2) Failover plan — if a primary site fails, how much state is lost during the RTO? I.e., do we accept any partial KV loss for 90s RTO?

We are happy to run the 48-hour sample — ops will share by EOD Friday.

Thanks,
Priya Shah
VP, Platform & Ops
BrightLane
From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
To: Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.com>, Priya Shah <priya@brightlane.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 8 Oct 2026 08:17:46 -0700
Subject: Re: Throughput commitments and cross-site egress choreography for BrightLane private GPU pools

Priya / Diego —

Short answers plus a small set of operational constraints to consider before we lock the SLA: 

On costs and control plane traffic:
- Control plane checks (health & metrics) are lightweight — these do not count toward customer egress billing. Heavy egress is model payload (token streams) and KV checkpoint replication between sites. We will provide an estimate table in the workbook once we have tokens/request distribution from the sample.

On failover semantics and state:
- Our design trades a bounded window of accepted-in-flight request loss for faster RTOs. For the 90s RTO target we recommend:
  * KV replication cadence: every 30s incremental checkpoints (async), cross-site push. This minimizes cold misses but does not guarantee zero-loss for requests in-flight at the moment of failure.
  * Warm pool replication: we keep warm pool indices in-memory and replicate metadata every 10s; warm cache hotness is probabilistic in the first 60–120s after failover.
  * Expected partial loss: under the recommended configuration, expect ~0–2% of requests to see partial reruns or truncated completions during the 90s window.

On bandwidth and sync behavior given your 6 Gbps carve-out:
- Baseline (20k tokens/s) with your 850 tokens/request -> ~23 RPS sustained. Most KV sync happens when new contexts ingest into models; estimate cross-site replication steady-state at ~1–1.5 Gbps with spikes to 3–4 Gbps during heavy checkpointing. 6 Gbps reserve is safe with room for other tenant noise.

Operational asks from BrightLane ops team:
1) Provide anonymized 48-hour traffic sample (tokens/request histogram + request timestamps) — we’ll run it through the attached capacity model.
2) Confirm whether you want stricter durability (zero in-flight loss) — if yes, we need to shift to synchronous replication (adds ~30% CPU and bandwidth) and RTO will likely increase to 3–5 minutes.

I will update capacity-model-v2.xlsx with an egress cost estimate row and a sync-mode comparison column by EOD today.

–Jonas
Director, Private Deployments
Redwood Inference

Priya —

Perfect, thanks for the answers and the carve-out commit. Action items and a short runbook attached so ops can walk through the validation steps this week. Highlighted plan below: 

Operational runbook (short):
1) Confirm egress /29 + announce (BrightLane ops) — target: Thu EOD.
2) Share anonymized 48-hour sample (csv + histogram) — target: Fri EOD (we will ingest and return modelled scenarios).
3) We (Redwood) will: update capacity-model-v2.xlsx with egress cost estimates and sync-mode tradeoffs; produce privgpu-failover-runbook.md (attached) with step-by-step failover drills and expected symptoms.
4) Dry run window: propose Mon 10/12 02:00–04:00 PST for a non-prod failover drill (we'll coordinate API keys and alerting).

Notes & constraints:
- If you choose synchronous replication for zero-loss, expect a 30% uplift in network and CPU; it will also push RTO to ~3–5 minutes — call this out to stakeholders.
- With your 6 Gbps carve-out and the attached settings we are confident we can meet the 20k tokens/s SLA with the 90s RTO. If traffic shape unexpectedly skews (tokens/request >> 2k), we should reevaluate pod size.

Next step: Priya/ops to confirm the egress announce + provide the 48h sample. Laura and I will schedule the handoff meeting and send calendar invites.

Thanks all —
Diego
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference
